abstract: β-defensin 130 is a potential antimicrobial peptide candidate against enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)-K88 infection, but its in vivo mechanism remains unclear. In this study, the antibacterial activity of β-defensin 130 against ETEC-K88 was first evaluated in vitro, and membrane damage was observed by morphological disruption and PI uptake. Then, an ETEC-K88-infected mouse model was established and treated with β-defensin 130. Based on 16 S rDNA sequencing and LC-MS metabolomics, ETEC-K88 infection was shown to reduce gut microbial diversity and alter community structure. Correlation analysis revealed significant microbiota-metabolite interactions, β-defensin 130 treatment was associated with increased gut microbial diversity and partial recovery of the gut microbial community, increased beneficial Bacteroidota/Firmicutes, decreased pathogenic Proteobacteria, and partial reversal of infection-associated metabolic disturbances (e.g., upregulating L-tryptophan and linoleic acid). Collectively, these findings suggest that β-defensin 130 may alleviate ETEC-K88 infection by disrupting bacterial membranes, modulating gut microbiota, and partially restoring metabolic homeostasis, supporting its further development as a potential antimicrobial agent.

summary: In ETEC-K88-infected mice, β-defensin 130 shifted gut microbiota toward Bacteroidota/Firmicutes and partially reversed LC-MS-detected metabolic disturbances.
title: β-defensin 130 Counteracts ETEC-K88 Infection in Mice: Mechanistic Insights from Gut Microbiome and LC-MS-Based Metabolomic Correlation Analysis.
